<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{Lemma:ConstantSheafProperties}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $Z \subseteq X$ be a non-empty locally closed set. 
Then the following are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $Z$ is irreducible; 
    \item $k_Z$ is uniform; 
    \item $k_Z$ is monoform. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
(i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (ii): 
Simply, 
\begin{align*}
    k_Z \text{ is uniform} 
    &\iff \text{ all non-zero subobjects of $k_Z$ have a non-zero intersection} \\
    &\iff \text{ all non-empty open subsets of $Z$ have a non-empty intersection (in $Z$)} \\
    &\iff Z \text{ is irreducible}. 
\end{align*}

(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iii): 
Assume that $Z$ is irreducible.
To show that $k_Z$ is monoform, let $U \subseteq X$ be an open subset such that $U \cap Z \not= \emptyset$ and suppose that $k_Z$ and $k_{Z} / k_{U \cap Z} = k_{Z \setminus U}$ admit a common subobject.
In other words, there exist open subsets $V,W \subseteq X$ such that $V \cap Z = W \cap (Z \setminus U)$. 
Suppose that $V \cap Z \neq \emptyset$. Since $Z$ is irreducible and both $U \cap Z$ and $V \cap Z$ are non-empty open subsets of $Z$, we obtain $U \cap V \cap Z \not= \emptyset$. 
However,
\[
  V \cap Z \cap U = (W \cap (Z \setminus U)) \cap U = \emptyset, 
\]
which is a contradiction. 
Therefore, $V \cap Z = \emptyset$, and hence, the only common subobject of $k_Z$ and $k_Z/k_{U \cap Z}$ is zero. 
Thus, $k_Z$ is monoform. 

(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) Every monoform object is also uniform.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{Lemma:SectionInduceMonomorf}
Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item If $U \subseteq X$ is open and $s \in \mathcal{F}(U)$ is a non-zero section, then there exist a non-zero monomorphism $k_{\operatorname{supp}(s)} \to \mathcal{F}$ whose image contains $s$; 

  \item If $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, then there exist a locally closed set $Z \subseteq X$ containing $x$ and a non-zero monomoprhism $k_Z \to \mathcal{F}$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
(i) The section $s$ generates a subsheaf, which is isomorphic with $k_{\operatorname{supp}(s)}$. 
Note that $k_{\operatorname{supp}(s)}$ is well-defined, because $\operatorname{supp}(s)$ is a locally closed set of $X$. 

(ii) If $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, then there exist an open subset $U \subseteq X$ containing $x$ and a non-zero section $s \in \mathcal{F}(U)$ such that $s_x \not= 0$. 
Now, apply (i) for the section $s$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{Rmk:SobPresProd}
Observe that, although the sobrification functor is a left adjoint, it preserves products. 
More precisely, if $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is a family of topological spaces, then
\[
  \operatorname{Sob} \left( \prod_{i \in I} X_i \right) = \prod_{i \in I} \operatorname{Sob}(X_i). 
\]
For more details, see \cite[Theorem 1.4]{sobrificationHoffmannRemainder}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{Rmk:SheavesOnSobEqv}
Recall that the category of sheaves is determined by the frame of open subsets $\operatorname{Open}(X)$ rather than by the topological space $X$ itself. 
More precisely, if $X_1$ and $X_2$ are topological spaces and $f \colon \operatorname{Open}(X_1) \to \operatorname{Open}(X_2)$ is an order-isomorphism, then it induces an equivalence of categories $\mathbf{Sh}(X_1) \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(X_2)$. 
In particular, this applies to a topological space $X$ and its sobrification: 
\[
  \mathbf{Sh}(X) \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)). 
\]
Consequently, we may always restrict our attention to sober topological spaces.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{Lemma:IndicatorSheafFlabbyForClosedIrred}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $Z \subseteq X$ be a closed and irreducible subset. 
Then $k_Z$ is flabby and indecomposable.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Firstly, $k_Z$ is uniform by Lemma \ref{Lemma:ConstantSheafProperties}, and hence, indecomposable. 
Secondly, the constant sheaf $k_Z$ on $Z$ is flabby, since every non-empty open subset of $Z$ is connected. 
The extension by zero along the closed inclusion $i \colon Z \to X$ coincides with the direct image functor. 
In particular, it preserves flabbiness. 
Hence, $k_Z$ is also flabby as a sheaf on $X$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{Prop:SheafHomSuppSky}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
Then $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{F}, \operatorname{sky}(x)) \not= 0$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
If $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, then $\mathcal{F}_x \not= 0$, so there exist a non-zero $k$-linear map $\mathcal{F}_x \to k$. 
This induces a non-zero morphism of sheaves $\mathcal{F} \to \operatorname{sky}(x)$. 
Suppose then that $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{F}, \operatorname{sky}(x)) \not= 0$. 
Then there exists a non-zero morphism $\varphi \colon \mathcal{F} \to \operatorname{sky}(x)$ and an open subset $U \subseteq X$ such that $\varphi_U \not= 0$. 
We have a commutative diagram 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
  \mathcal{F}(U) \arrow{r}{\varphi_U} \arrow{d} & \operatorname{sky}(x)(U) \arrow{d} \\
  \mathcal{F}_x \arrow{r}{\varphi_x} & \operatorname{sky}(x)_x
\end{tikzcd}
\]
From this we can see that the non-zero morphism $\mathcal{F}(U) \to \operatorname{sky}(x)_x$ factors through $\mathcal{F}_x$. 
Thus, $\mathcal{F}_x \not= 0$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{Prop:IndInjSuppIrr}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
If $\mathcal{F}$ is uniform, then $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ is irreducible. 
In particular, if $\mathcal{F}$ is indecomposable injective sheaf on $X$, 
then $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ is irreducible.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $U_1, U_2 \subseteq X$ be open subsets such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \cap U_1$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \cap U_2$ are non-empty. 
In particular, there exist points $x_1 \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \cap U_1$ and $x_2 \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \cap U_2$. 
Consider the subsheaves $\mathcal{F}_{U_1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{U_2}$ of $\mathcal{F}$. 
These are non-zero, since $(\mathcal{F}_{U_i})_{x_i} = \mathcal{F}_{x_i} \not= 0$ for $i = 1,2$. 
As non-zero subsheaves of the uniform sheaf $\mathcal{F}$, their intersection must also be non-zero. 
However, their intersection is precisely $\mathcal{F}_{U_1 \cap U_2}$. 
Thus, $\mathcal{F}_y = (\mathcal{F}_{U_1 \cap U_2})_y \not= 0$ for some $y \in U_1 \cap U_2$ proving the first claim. 

Finally, every indecomposable injective object is uniform; see, for example, \cite[p.~296]{popescu}. This proves the second claim.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{Pro:IndInjShIsGeneratedByAGlobalSec}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be an indecomposable injective sheaf on $X$. 
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is generated by a global section i.e.\ 
there exists a non-zero global section $s \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ such that $\mathcal{F} = \langle s \rangle$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Take any non-zero global section $s \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ (such a section exists since $\mathcal{F}$ is non-zero and flabby). This section generates a subsheaf $\langle s \rangle$ of $\mathcal{F}$. The support of this subsheaf is $\operatorname{supp}(s)$ and, in particular, is closed.
Observe that $\langle s \rangle$ is uniform, as a subobject of the uniform sheaf $\mathcal{F}$. Hence, by Lemma \ref{Lemma:ConstantSheafProperties}, the support $\operatorname{supp}(s)$ is irreducible. It follows from Lemma \ref{Lemma:IndicatorSheafFlabbyForClosedIrred} that $\langle s \rangle$ is flabby, and therefore injective.
Consequently, the exact sequence $0 \to \langle s \rangle \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F} / \langle s \rangle \to 0$ splits. 
Since $\mathcal{F}$ is indecomposable, we must have either $\langle s \rangle = 0$ or $\langle s \rangle = \mathcal{F}$. As $s \neq 0$, the first possibility is excluded. Therefore, $ \mathcal{F} = \langle s \rangle$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{Prop:IndInjSuppClosed}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be an indecomposable injective sheaf on $X$. 
Then the support of $\mathcal{F}$ is closed.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Pro:IndInjShIsGeneratedByAGlobalSec}, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) = \operatorname{supp}(s)$ for some non-zero global section $s \in \mathcal{F}(X)$. 
Thus, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ is closed.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{Thm:IndInjAreSkysrc}
Let $X$ be a sober topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
Then $\mathcal{F}$ is indecomposable injective if and only if $\mathcal{F} \cong \operatorname{sky}(x)$ for some $x \in X$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Pro:IndInjShIsGeneratedByAGlobalSec}, there exists a non-zero global section $s \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ such that $\mathcal{F} = \langle s \rangle$. 
The support of $\mathcal{F}$ is irreducible and closed by Propositions \ref{Prop:IndInjSuppIrr} and \ref{Prop:IndInjSuppClosed}. 
Since $X$ is sober, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) = \operatorname{supp}(s) = \overline{ \{ x \}}$ for some $x \in X$. 
Hence, we obtain an isomorphism  
\[
  \mathcal{F} = \langle s \rangle \cong k_{\operatorname{supp}(s)} = k_{\overline{ \{ x \} } } = \operatorname{sky}(x)
\]
for some $x \in X$. 

The converse was shown in Lemma \ref{Lemma:IndicatorSheafFlabbyForClosedIrred}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{Cor:IndInjAreIrredClosed}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
There is a one-to-one correspondence with the indecomposable injective sheaves on $X$ and the points of the sobrification of $X$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
By definition, $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$ is sober topological space, so by the previous theorem, there is a one-to-one correspondence with the points of $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$  
and indecoposable injective sheaves on $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$. 
But recall from Remark \ref{Rmk:SheavesOnSobEqv} that there is an equivalence of categories, $\mathbf{Sh}(X) \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\operatorname{Sob}(X))$. 
Thus, the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{Rmk:Hoppner}
Corollary \ref{Cor:IndInjAreIrredClosed} may be viewed as a partial generalization of Höppner's classification of indecomposable injective persistence modules \cite[Proposition 1.1]{Hoppner}.
Let $P$ be a poset. 
Höppner showed that the indecomposable injective persistence modules over $P$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the upward-directed down-sets $D \subseteq P$.
This connection can be made more explicit by expressing these order-theoretic properties in topological terms. 
Recall that the category of persistence modules over $P$ is equivalent to $\mathbf{Sh}(P^a)$, and that a subset $D \subseteq P$ is upward-directed (resp.\ a down-set) if and only if it is irreducible (resp.\ closed) with respect to the Alexandrov topology.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{Prop:OneSideInverseForSuppSets}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $Z \subseteq X$ be Skula-open. 
Then 
\[
  Z = (\operatorname{Supp} \circ \operatorname{Supp}^{-1})(Z). 
\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
First, recall that $(\operatorname{Supp} \circ \operatorname{Supp}^{-1})(Z) \subseteq Z$ for every subset $Z \subseteq X$. 
Let $x \in Z$. 
Since $Z$ is Skula-open, there exists a locally closed subset $Z_x \subseteq Z$ containing $x$. Consider the constant sheaf $k_{Z_x}$ on $Z_x$ and its extension by zero $i_!k_{Z_x}$ to $X$, where $i \colon Z_x \to X$ is the inclusion. 
By definition, $\operatorname{Supp}(i_! k_{Z_x}) = Z_x \subseteq Z$, so $i_! k_{Z_x} \in \operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z)$. 
Moreover, since $(i_! k_{Z_x})_x \not= 0$, we conclude that $x \in (\operatorname{Supp} \circ \operatorname{Supp}^{-1})(Z)$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{Prop:SkulaOpenCorrespondsSupports}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $Z \subseteq X$. 
Then the following are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $Z$ is Skula-open; 
    \item $Z = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ for some sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$; 
    \item $Z = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$ for some localizing subcategory $\mathcal{L}$ of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
(ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i): 
Suppose that $Z = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ for some sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$. 
We know that 
\[
  \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) = \bigcup_{U}\bigcup_{s \in \mathcal{F}(U)} \operatorname{supp}(s).
\]
Therefore, $Z$ is Skula-open as a union of locally closed subsets. 


(iii) $\Rightarrow$ (ii): 
Assume that $Z = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$ for some localizing subcategory $\mathcal{L}$ of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$. For each $x \in Z$, choose a sheaf $\mathcal{F}(x) \in \mathcal{L}$ such that $\mathcal{F}(x)_x \not= 0$. 
Consider the direct sum $\mathcal{F} = \bigoplus_{x \in Z} \mathcal{F}(x)$. 
By construction, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}) \subseteq \bigcup_{x \in Z} \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}(x)) = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$. 
Conversely, as a localizing subcategory, $\mathcal{L}$ is closed under direct sums, so $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L}$. 
In particular, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$. 
Thus, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}) = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$. 

(i) $\Rightarrow$ (iii): 
Finally, suppose that $Z$ is Skula-open. 
By Proposition \ref{Prop:OneSideInverseForSuppSets}, $Z = \operatorname{Supp}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z))$. 
Hence, we may take $\mathcal{L} = \operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z)$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{Rmk:SkulaOpenByLocSubCat}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
We now have a Galois connection, where $\operatorname{Supp}$ is surjective: 
\[
  \{ \text{Localizing subcategories of } \mathbf{Sh}(X) \} \xrightleftharpoons[\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}]{\operatorname{Supp}} \{ \text{Skula-open subsets of } X \}. 
\]
However, it is not always a bijection. 
Consider, for example, the space $X = \mathbb{R}$ with the Alexandrov topology. 
Then the full subcategory of ephemeral modules $\mathbf{Eph}$ is a (bi)localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(\mathbb{R})$ (see Section \ref{Sec:ApplicationsToTDA}). 
The sheaf supported by a singleton $k_x$ is in $\mathbf{Eph}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. 
Thus, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathbf{Eph}) = \mathbb{R}$. 
Obviously, the whole $\mathbf{Sh}(\mathbb{R})$ is a localizing subcategory of itself, and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathbf{Sh}(\mathbb{R})) = \mathbb{R}$. 
Therefore, $\operatorname{Supp}$ cannot be an injection in the case of $X = \mathbb{R}$. 
For more details, see \cite{EphModAndScottShOverContPoset}.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{Prop:SkyContMap}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
Then 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item 
    $\operatorname{sky}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})) = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$ for all localizing subcategories $\mathcal{L}$ of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$; 

    \item 
    $\operatorname{sky}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z))) = Z$ for all Skula-open subsets $Z \subseteq X$; 

    \item 
    $\operatorname{sky} \colon \operatorname{Sk}(X) \to \operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is continuous. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
(i) 
By Proposition \ref{Prop:SheafHomSuppSky}, 
\begin{align*}
    x \in \operatorname{sky}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})) 
    &\iff \operatorname{sky}(x) \in \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L}) \\
    &\iff \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{F}, \operatorname{sky}(x)) \not= 0 \text{ for some } \mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L} \\
    &\iff x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \text{ for some } \mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L} \\
    &\iff x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}). 
\end{align*}

(ii) 
This is a consequence of (i) and Proposition \ref{Prop:OneSideInverseForSuppSets}:
\[
  \operatorname{sky}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z))) = \operatorname{Supp}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(Z)) = Z. 
\]

(iii) 
This follows from (i) and Proposition \ref{Prop:SkulaOpenCorrespondsSupports}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{Prop:SuppAndASuppConnection}
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
Then the following are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$; 

    \item $\operatorname{sky}(x) \in \mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})))$; 

    \item $\overline{\operatorname{sky}(x)} \in \operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F})$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
(i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (ii) : 
By Proposition \ref{Prop:SkyContMap} (ii), 
\[
    \operatorname{sky}(x) \in \mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))) 
    \iff x \in \operatorname{sky}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})))) = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\]

(i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iii) : 
Recall that $\operatorname{ASupp}(M) = \{ \overline{H} \in \operatorname{ASpec}(\mathcal{G}) \mid \operatorname{Hom}(M, E(H)) \not= 0 \}$ for all objects $M \in \mathcal{G}$. 
Thus, the claim follows from Proposition \ref{Prop:SheafHomSuppSky}: 
\[
  x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) 
  \iff \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{F}, \operatorname{sky}(x)) \not= 0 
  \iff \overline{\operatorname{sky}(x)} \in \operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F}). 
\]
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{Prop:AtomToGabrielBijectionSober}
Let $X$ be a sober topological space. 
Then the map $\overline{E} \colon \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \to \operatorname{InjSpec}(X)$ is a bijection.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The map is always an injection. 
By Theorem \ref{Thm:IndInjAreSkysrc}, $\operatorname{InjSpec}(X)$ consists of the skyscraper sheaves $\operatorname{sky}(x)$, where $x \in X$. 
The skyscraper sheaf $\operatorname{sky}(x)$ is monoform (Lemma \ref{Lemma:IndicatorSheafFlabbyForClosedIrred}) and injective, so $\overline{E}(\overline{\operatorname{sky}(x)}) = E(\operatorname{sky}(x)) = \operatorname{sky}(x)$ proving the surjectivity.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{Prop:AtomToGabrielContSober}
Let $X$ be a sober topological space, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$. Then $\overline{E}^{-1}(\mathcal O(\mathcal L))$ is atom-open. More precisely,
$\overline{E}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})) = \operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F})$ for some $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L}$. 
In other words, $\overline{E} \colon \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \to \operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is a continuous map.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Prop:SkulaOpenCorrespondsSupports},  
$\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}) = \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ for some sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$. 
Now, by Propositions \ref{Prop:SkyContMap} (i) and \ref{Prop:SuppAndASuppConnection}, 
\begin{align*}
  \overline{\operatorname{sky}(x)} \in \overline{E}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})) 
  &\iff \operatorname{sky}(x) \in \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L}) \\
  &\iff x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}) \\
  &\iff x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \\
  &\iff \overline{\operatorname{sky}(x)} \in \operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F}). 
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{Prop:EIsOpenMapCaseSober}
Let $X$ be a sober topological space, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X$. 
Then $\overline{E}(\operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F})) = \mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})))$. 
In particular, $\overline{E} \colon \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \to \operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is an open map.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Prop:SuppAndASuppConnection}, $\overline{E}^{-1}(\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})))) = \operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F})$. 
Since $\overline{E}$ is a bijection by Proposition \ref{Prop:AtomToGabrielBijectionSober}, we also have $\overline{E}(\operatorname{ASupp}(\mathcal{F})) = \mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})))$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{Thm:AtomSpecHomeoGabriel}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
Then the atom spectrum and the Gabriel spectrum are homeomorphic: 
\[
  \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(X). 
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Suppose first that $X$ is sober. 
By Proposition~\ref{Prop:AtomToGabrielBijectionSober}, the map 
$\overline{E} \colon \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \to \operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is a bijection. 
Moreover, it is continuous by Proposition~\ref{Prop:AtomToGabrielContSober} and open by Proposition~\ref{Prop:EIsOpenMapCaseSober}. Hence \(\overline{E}\) is a homeomorphism.

Now let $X$ be arbitrary. By Remark \ref{Rmk:SheavesOnSobEqv}, there is an equivalence of  categories $\mathbf{Sh}(X) \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\operatorname{Sob}(X))$. Therefore
\[
  \operatorname{ASpec}(X) \approx \operatorname{ASpec}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(X),
\]
where the middle homeomorphism follows from the sober case.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{Prop:SkyInjBij}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item 
    If $X$ is $T_0$, then $\operatorname{sky} \colon X \to \operatorname{InjSpec}(X)$ an injection; 

    \item 
    If $X$ is sober, then $\operatorname{sky} \colon X \to \operatorname{InjSpec}(X)$ a bijection. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
(i) 
Recall that in a $T_0$-space, we have an equivalence: 
\[
  \overline{\{ x \}} = \overline{\{ y \} } \iff x = y. 
\]
Thus, $\operatorname{sky}(x) = \operatorname{sky}(y)$ if and only if $x = y$. 

(ii) 
Every sober space is $T_0$, so the injectivity follows from (i). 
The surjectivity follows from Theorem \ref{Thm:IndInjAreSkysrc}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{Thm:ForSobSpaceGabrielIsSkula}
Let $X$ be a sober topological space. 
Then there exist a homeomorphism for the Gabriel spectrum: 
\[
   \operatorname{Sp}(X) \approx \operatorname{Sk}(X). 
\]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Since the map $\operatorname{sky} \colon \operatorname{Sk}(X) \to \operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is a bijection by Proposition \ref{Prop:SkyInjBij} (ii), it follows from Proposition \ref{Prop:SkyContMap} that $\operatorname{sky}(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})) = \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})$ for all localizing subcategories $\mathcal{L}$ of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$. 
In other words, $\operatorname{sky}$ is an open map, in addition being a continuous bijection. 
Thus, it is a homeomorphism.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
Then there exists a homeomorphism for the Gabriel spectrum: 
\[
   \operatorname{Sp}(X) \approx \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)). 
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Note that there is an equivalence of sheaf categories $\mathbf{Sh}(X) \simeq \mathbf{Sh}(\operatorname{Sob}(X))$ (see Remark \ref{Rmk:SheavesOnSobEqv}). 
Thus, 
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}(X) 
  \approx \operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)) 
  \approx \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)). 
\]
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{Thm:GabrielSpectrumTopProperties}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
Then the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item is Hausdorff; 
    \item admits a basis of clopen subsets; 
    \item is zero-dimensional with respect to the small inductive dimension; 
    \item is totally disconnected. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
(i) 
It is known that the Skula topology of a $T_0$-space is Hausdorff \cite[Exercise 9.7.16]{goubault-larrecq_2013}. 
Since the sobrification $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$ is always a $T_0$-space, it follows that $\operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X))$ is Hausdorff. 
Corollary~\ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob} therefore implies that $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is Hausdorff.

 

(ii)
The Skula topology admits a basis of clopen subsets \cite[p.~146]{sobrificationHoffmannRemainder}. Hence the claim follows from Corollary~\ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}.


(iii) and (iv) 
Both statements are immediate consequences of (ii).
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{Thm:ProductOfGabrielSpectrums}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. 
Then $\operatorname{Sp}(X \times Y) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(X) \times \operatorname{Sp}(Y)$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
The Skula topology respects the product topology: $\operatorname{Sk}(X \times Y) = \operatorname{Sk}(X) \times \operatorname{Sk}(Y)$ (\cite[Lemma 1.2]{sobrificationHoffmannRemainder}). 
Now, by Remark \ref{Rmk:SobPresProd} and Corollary \ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}, 
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}(X \times Y) 
  \approx \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X \times Y)) 
  = \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X)) \times \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(Y)) 
  \approx \operatorname{Sp}(X) \times  \operatorname{Sp}(Y). 
\]
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{Thm:GabrielSpecCompact}
Let $X$ be a topological space. 
Then the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is compact if and only if $X$ is a Noetherian space.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Hoffmann proved that $\operatorname{Sk}(Y)$ is compact if and only if $Y$ is sober and Noetherian \cite[Theorem~3.1]{sobrificationHoffmannRemainder}. By Corollary~\ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}, there is a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Sp}(X)\cong \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(X))$. Since $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$ is always sober, it follows that $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is compact if and only if $\operatorname{Sob}(X)$ is Noetherian. Finally, a topological space is Noetherian if and only if its sobrification is Noetherian. Hence $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is compact if and only if $X$ is Noetherian.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{Thm:GabrielForHausdorff}
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff space. 
Then the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is discrete (with cardinality $\left\lvertX\right\rvert$).
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Since $X$ is Hausdorff, it is sober. Hence, by Theorem \ref{Thm:ForSobSpaceGabrielIsSkula}, $\operatorname{Sp}(X) \cong \operatorname{Sk}(X)$.
Moreover, every singleton of $X$ is closed, and therefore Skula-open. It follows that every singleton is open in $\operatorname{Sk}(X)$, so $\operatorname{Sk}(X)$ is discrete. Consequently, $\operatorname{Sp}(X)$ is also discrete.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{Prop:BasisOfSkulaOfContPoset}
Let $P$ be a continuous poset. 
Then the Skula topology of $P^{\sigma}$ has a basis consisting of sets $\operatorname{Int} U_x \cap D_y$, where $x,y \in P$. 
In particular, if $P = \mathbb{R}^n$, this basis consists of the rectangles \[ ]x_1, y_1] \times \dots \times \left] x_n, y_n \right]\] where
$x_i, y_i \in \mathbb{R}$ for all $i = 1, \dots, n$.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Recall that the collection of sets $\operatorname{Int} U_x$ $(x\in P)$ forms a basis for the Scott topology. Moreover, every down-set $D\subseteq P$ can be written as a union of basic down-sets, 
\[ 
  D=\bigcup_{y\in D} D_y, 
\] 
and each $D_y$ is Scott-closed. 
Since the Skula topology is generated by the Scott-open subsets together with the Scott-closed subsets, it follows that $\operatorname{Sk}(P^\sigma)$ admits a basis consisting of the sets $\operatorname{Int} U_x \cap D_y$, where $x,y\in P$. 
For $\bm{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $\bm{y}=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we have 
\[
  \operatorname{Int} U_{\bm{x}} = \left]x_1,\infty\right[\times\cdots\times\left]x_n,\infty\right[ 
  \quad \text{and} \quad  
  D_{\bm{y}} = \left]-\infty,y_1\right]\times\cdots\times\left]-\infty,y_n\right]. 
\] 
Therefore, 
\[ 
  \operatorname{Int} U_{\bm{x}}\cap D_{\bm{y}} = \left]x_1,y_1\right]\times\cdots\times\left]x_n,y_n\right], 
\] 
which proves the second claim.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
Note that the Sorgenfrey topology on $\mathbb{R}$ is often defined as the topology generated by the half-open intervals $[x,y[$, where $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$. 
This \emph{Sorgenfrey line} is clearly homeomorphic to the space considered in the previous proposition for $n = 1$. 
In this article, we use the former definition for the Sorgenfrey topology instead, since it is the one related to the Scott topology on $\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{Thm:GabrielSpecOfPerModOverR}
Let $P = \mathbb{R}^n$. Then there is a homeomorphism  
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbf{Vect})) \approx \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}^n)
\]
where $\operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is endowed with the topology generated by the rectangles \[\left] F_1, F_1' \right] \times \dots \times \left] F_{n}, F_{n}' \right],\] for $F_i,F_i' \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R})$ ($i = 1, \dots, {n}$).
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
We identify persistence modules over $\mathbb{R}^n$ with sheaves on $(\mathbb{R}^n)^a$. 

First consider the case $n = 1$.
The proper non-empty open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^a$ are precisely $\left[x, \infty \right[$ and $\left] x, \infty \right[$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. 
The corresponding open subsets in the sobrification $\operatorname{Sob}(\mathbb{R}^a)$ are 
\[
  \diamond \left[x, \infty \right[ 
  = \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid \left]-\infty, x \right] \subseteq F \} 
  = \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid \left]-\infty, x \right[ \subsetneq F \} 
\]
and 
\[
  \diamond \left]x, \infty \right[ 
  = \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid \left]-\infty, x \right] \subsetneq F \}. 
\]
The closed subsets are their complements, namely 
\[
  \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid F \subseteq \left] -\infty, x \right[ \}
  \quad \text{and} \quad 
  \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid F \subseteq \left] -\infty, x \right] \}. 
\]
The Skula topology of $\operatorname{Sob}(\mathbb{R}^a)$ is therefore generated by the sets 
\[
  \left] F_1, F_2 \right] = \{ F \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}) \mid F_1 \subsetneq F \subseteq F_2 \}, 
\]
where $F_1, F_2 \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R})$. 
The claim now follows from Corollary \ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}. 

We now turn to the general case.
Recall that the Alexandrov topology preserves products. 
In particular, $(\mathbb{R}^n)^a = (\mathbb{R}^a)^n$ for all $n \ge 1$. 
Therefore, the case $n=1$, together with Theorem \ref{Thm:ProductOfGabrielSpectrums}, yields 
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbf{Vect})) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Vect}))^n \approx \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R})^n = \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}^n), 
\]
where $\operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is endowed with corresponding product topology. 
This topology has a basis that consists of the rectangles $\left] F_1, F_1' \right] \times \dots \times \left] F_{n}, F_{n}' \right]$, where $F_i,F_i' \in \operatorname{Idl}(\mathbb{R})$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{Thm:GabrielSpecOfScottShOverR}
Let $P = \mathbb{R}^{n}$. 
Then there is a homeomorphism  
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}((\mathbb{R}^n)^{\sigma}) \approx (\mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \})^n, 
\]
where $(\mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \})^n$ is endowed with the product Sorgenfrey topology, that is, the topology generated by the rectangles \[ ]x_1,y_1]\times\cdots\times ]x_n,y_n], \] with $x_i\in\mathbb{R}$ and $y_i\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Let us first consider the case $n = 1$. 
The sobrification of $\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}$ is $(\mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \})^{\sigma}$ as the smallest sober space containing $\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}$. 
By Proposition \ref{Prop:BasisOfSkulaOfContPoset}, its Skula topology is generated by the intervals $\left] x, y \right]$, for $x < y$.
Corollary~\ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob} therefore yields $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbb{R}^\sigma) \approx \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ endowed with the Sorgenfrey topology.

For the general case, recall that the Scott topology preserves products of continuous posets \cite[Proposition 5.1.54]{goubault-larrecq_2013}. 
Hence, $(\mathbb{R}^n)^{\sigma} = (\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})^n$ for all $n \ge 1$. 
Thus, by Theorem \ref{Thm:ProductOfGabrielSpectrums}, 
\[
  \operatorname{Sp}((\mathbb{R}^n)^{\sigma}) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})^n \approx (\mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \})^n, 
\]
where the right-hand side is endowed with the product Sorgenfrey topology. Equivalently, its topology is generated by the boxes \[ ]x_1,y_1]\times\cdots\times ]x_n,y_n]. \]
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{Rmk:Embedding}
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a Grothendieck category. 
If $\mathcal{L}$ is a localizing subcategory of $\mathcal{G}$, then both $\mathcal{L}$ and the quotient category $\mathcal{G} / \mathcal{L}$ are Grothendieck categories. 
An indecomposable injective object of $\mathcal L$ is uniform when regarded as an object of $\mathcal G$, and therefore its injective envelope in $\mathcal G$ is an indecomposable injective object of $\mathcal G$. This defines an injective map
$\operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathcal{L}) \to \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathcal{G})$. 
The image of this map is precisely the Gabriel open set $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})$. 
Consequently, $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{L})$ is homeomorphic to an open subspace of $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{G})$. 
Similarly, the section functor $\sec \colon \mathcal{G} / \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{G}$ preserves indecomposable injective objects, and therefore induces an injective map $\operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathcal{G} / \mathcal{L}) \to \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathcal{G})$. 
The image of this map is the complementary Gabriel closed subset $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathcal{G}) \setminus \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{L})$. 
For more details, see, for example, \cite[Corollary 2.2.18]{KrauseHomTheoryRep}. 

In the situation $\mathcal{G} = \operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{Vect})$ and $\mathcal{L} = \mathbf{Eph}$, where $P$ is a continuous poset, it then follows that $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbf{Eph})$ is homeomorphic to an open subspace of $\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{Vect}))$, whereas $\operatorname{Sp}(P^{\sigma})$ is homeomorphic to the complementary closed subspace.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{Prop:GabrielSpecOfDenseLinPoset}
Let $P = \mathbb{R}$. Then $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbf{Eph})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}$ endowed with discrete topology.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By Remark \ref{Rmk:Embedding}, $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbf{Eph})$ is homeomorphic to the open set $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{\mathbf{Eph}})$ of $\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Vect}))$. The injective spectrum of
$\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Vect})$ consists of the interval modules $k\left] -\infty, p \right]$ and $k\left] -\infty, p \right[$, where $p\in \mathbb{R}$, together with the constant module $k[\mathbb{R}]$.
Recall that a persistence module $M\in \operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Vect})$ is ephemeral if and only if all its internal morphisms are zero. A direct calculation shows that \[\operatorname{Hom}(M, k\left] -\infty, p \right])=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_p,k)\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{Hom}(M, k\left] -\infty, p \right[])=0.\] Moreover,  
$\operatorname{Hom}(M, k[\mathbb{R}]) = 0$. Therefore 
\[\mathcal{O}(\mathbf{Eph}) = \{ k\left] -\infty, p \right] \mid p \in \mathbb{R} \}\] 
Furthermore,
\[\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}(\{p\})) = \{ k\left] -\infty, p \right] \}\] for all $p \in \mathbb{R}$.
Hence every point $k\left] -\infty, p \right]$ is open in $\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Vect}))$.
Thus $\mathcal O(\mathbf{Eph})$ is a discrete subspace. Since its points are naturally parametrized by $\mathbb{R}$, it follows that $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbf{Eph})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}$ endowed with the discrete topology.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a linearly ordered poset. 
Then the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(P^{\sigma})$ is compact if and only if $P$ is well-ordered.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Recall that a linearly ordered poset $P$ is well-ordered, or equivalently Artinian, if and only if $P^\sigma$ is a Noetherian space. The claim therefore follows from Theorem~\ref{Thm:GabrielSpecCompact}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a continuous poset. 
Then 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item a singleton $\{ p \}$ $(p \in P)$ is Skula-open in the Scott topology if and only if $p$ is compact; 
    \item $P$ is Noetherian if and only if $P$ is a dcpo and $p$ is compact for all $p \in P$; 
    \item $P$ is Noetherian if and only if $\operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma})$ is Noetherian as a poset; 
    \item the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(P^{\sigma})$ is discrete if and only if $P$ is a Noetherian poset. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
(i) 
Simply, 
\[
  \{ p \} \text{ is Skula-open} 
  \iff U_p \text{ is Scott-open} 
  \iff p \ll p 
  \iff p \text{ is compact}.
\]

(ii)
See \cite[Remark 2.1]{li2026conoetherianspaces}. 

(iii)
Note that $P$ is a subposet of $\operatorname{Sob}(P^\sigma)$. Hence, if $\operatorname{Sob}(P^\sigma)$ is Noetherian, then so is $P$. Conversely, if $P$ is Noetherian, then $P$ is  dcpo by (ii). We then know by \cite[Proposition 8.2.12]{goubault-larrecq_2013} that $P^\sigma$ is sober, and therefore $\operatorname{Sob}(P^\sigma)=P$. Hence $\operatorname{Sob}(P^\sigma)$ is a Noetherian poset.

(iv) By \cite[Exercise 8.2.48]{goubault-larrecq_2013} the topological space $\operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma})$ is the Scott space of the underlying poset, which coincides with the so-called rounded ideal completion.  Moreover, we know by \cite{goubault-larrecq_2013} that this poset is always a dcpo. The claim now follows from Corollary \ref{Cor:GabrielIsSkulaSob}, (i), (ii) and (iii): 
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Sp}(P^{\sigma}) \text{ is discrete} 
  &\iff \operatorname{Sk}(\operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma})) \text{ is discrete} \\
  &\iff \text{every point of } \operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma}) \text{ is Skula-open} \\
  &\iff \text{every point of } \operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma}) \text{ is compact} \\
  &\iff \operatorname{Sob}(P^{\sigma}) \text{ is a Noetherian poset} \\
  &\iff P \text{ is a Noetherian poset}. 
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(X)$. 
Then $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$ if and only if $k_Z \in \mathcal{L}$ for some locally closed set $Z$ containing $x$.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
If $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$, then $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ for some $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L}$. 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma:SectionInduceMonomorf} (ii), there exists a locally closed subset $Z \subseteq X$ and a monomorphism $k_Z \to \mathcal{F}$. 
Since $\mathcal{L}$ is closed under subobjects, it follows that $k_Z \in \mathcal{L}$.

Conversely, if $k_Z \in \mathcal{L}$ for some locally closed subset
$Z$ containing $x$, then $x \in \operatorname{Supp}(k_Z) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{Lemma:PointInSupportImpliesInterval2}
Let $P$ be a continuous poset and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(P^{\sigma})$. 
Then $p \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$ if and only if $j_*k[x,p] \in \mathcal{L}$ for some $x \ll p$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Suppose first that $p \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$. By the previous proposition,
$j_*k[I] \in \mathcal{L}$ for some locally Scott-closed interval
$I \subseteq P$ containing $p$.
In particular, $\operatorname{Int} U_x \cap D_p \subseteq I$ for some $x \ll p$.
Therefore, $j_*k[x,p]$ is a subquotient of $j_*k[I]$, and hence $j_*k[x,p] \in \mathcal{L}$.

Conversely, if $j_*k[x, p] \in \mathcal{L}$ for some $x \ll p$, then $p \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$, because $j_*k[x,p]_p = k \not= 0$, 
so $p \in \operatorname{Supp}(j_*k[x,p]) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{Prop:IndicatorsInLocalizingSubcategory3}
Let $P = \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(P^{\sigma})$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item If $p, q \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$ such that $p \ll q$ and $\left] p, q \right] \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$, then $j_*k[p,q] \in \mathcal{L}$; 

    \item If $I \subseteq \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$ is a locally Scott-closed interval such that $I \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$, then $j_*k[I] \in \mathcal{L}$.  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
(i) 
Consider the set
\[
  A = \{ x \in [p,q] \mid j_*k[x,q] \in \mathcal{L} \}.
\]
First, $A$ is non-empty, since $q \in A$ (indeed, $j_*k[q,q]=0\in\mathcal{L}$). Moreover, $A$ is bounded below. Hence, by the completeness of $\mathbb{R}$, $A$ has an infimum, which we denote by $a = \inf A$.

We first show that $j_*k[a,q] \in \mathcal{L}$. Since $a = \inf A$, every point $x$ satisfying $a < x \le q$ belongs to $A$. 
Thus, $j_*k[x,q] \in \mathcal{L}$ for every $a < x \le q$. 
These sheaves form a directed system $(j_*k[x,q])_{a < x \le q}$, and
\[
  j_*k[a,q] = \varinjlim_{a < x \le q} j_*k[x,q].
\]
Since $\mathcal{L}$ is closed under direct limits as a localizing subcategory, it follows that
$j_*k[a,q]\in\mathcal{L}$. 
In particular, $a \in A$. 

It remains to prove that $a = p$. 
Suppose, to the contrary, that $a > p$. 
Then $a \in \left] p,q \right] \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$.
By Lemma \ref{Lemma:PointInSupportImpliesInterval2}, there exists $y < a$ such that $j_*k[y,a] \in \mathcal{L}$.
Since
$\left] y, q \right] = \left] y, a \right] \cup \left] a , q \right]$, there is a short exact sequence
\[
  0 \to j_*k[a,q] \to j_*k[y, q] \to j_*k[y,a] \to 0. 
\]
Because $\mathcal{L}$ is closed under extensions, $j_*k[y,q]\in\mathcal{L}$. 
Hence $y \in A$, contradicting the fact that $a = \inf A$, since $y < a$.
Therefore $p = a \in A$, and consequently $j_*k[p,q]\in\mathcal{L}$.

(ii) 
By the previous item, the claim has already been established for all bounded locally Scott-closed intervals. Thus, it remains only to consider the unbounded intervals $I= \left] -\infty , q \right]$, where $q\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$.

For every $x\in I$, we have
\[
  \left] x,q \right] \subseteq I \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal L).
\]
Hence, (i) yields $j_*k[x,q]\in\mathcal L$.
Moreover, the sheaves $(j_*k[x,q])_{x\in I}$ form a directed system, and
\[
  j_*k[I] = \varinjlim_{x\in I}j_*k[x,q].
\]
Since $\mathcal L$ is closed under direct limits, it follows that $j_*k[I]\in\mathcal L$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{Thm:OneSideInverseForLocSubCat}
Let $P = \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a localizing subcategory of $\mathbf{Sh}(P^{\sigma})$. 
Then 
\[
  \mathcal{L} = (\operatorname{Supp}^{-1} \circ \operatorname{Supp})(\mathcal{L}). 
\]
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Recall first that $\mathcal{L} \subseteq (\operatorname{Supp}^{-1} \circ \operatorname{Supp})(\mathcal{L})$. 
Suppose now that $\mathcal{F} \in (\operatorname{Supp}^{-1} \circ \operatorname{Supp})(\mathcal{L})$. 
Equivalently, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L})$. 
Fix $p \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ and a non-zero germ $s_p \in \mathcal{F}_p$. 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma:SectionInduceMonomorf}, there exist a locally Scott-closed interval $I_{s,p} \subseteq P$ that contains $p$ and a morphism $\varphi \colon j_*k[I_{s,p}] \to \mathcal{F}$, where $\varphi_p(1) = s_p \not= 0$. 
Thus, 
\[
  I_{s,p} = \operatorname{supp}(s) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F}) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{L}). 
\]
It follows from Proposition \ref{Prop:IndicatorsInLocalizingSubcategory3} (ii) that $j_*k[I_{s,p}] \in \mathcal{L}$. 
Repeating this construction for every non-zero germ at $p$ yields a morphism
\[
  \bigoplus_{0 \not= s_p \in \mathcal{F}_p} j_*k[I_{s,p}] \to \mathcal{F}
\]
that is surjective on the stalk at $p$. 
Taking the direct sum over all points of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, we obtain an epimorphism 
\[
  \bigoplus_{p \in \operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal{F})} \bigoplus_{0 \not= s_p \in \mathcal{F}_p} j_*k[I_{s,p}] \to \mathcal{F}. 
\]
Since $\mathcal{L}$ is closed under arbitrary direct sums, the domain of this morphism is in $\mathcal{L}$. 
As $\mathcal{L}$ is also closed under quotients, it follows that $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{L}$.
Hence, $(\operatorname{Supp}^{-1} \circ \operatorname{Supp})(\mathcal{L}) \subseteq \mathcal{L}$. Together with the reverse inclusion, this proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{Cor:LocalizingSubCatAndSkulaOpenR}
Let $P = \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$. 
Then there are one-to-one correspondences 
\[
  \left\{ \begin{tabular}{c} Localizing \\ subcategories of $\mathbf{Sh}(P^{\sigma})$ \end{tabular}  \right\} 
  \xrightleftharpoons[\operatorname{Supp}^{-1}]{\operatorname{Supp}}  
  \left\{ \begin{tabular}{c} Skula-open \\ sets of $P^{\sigma}$ \end{tabular}  \right\} 
  \xrightleftharpoons[\operatorname{sky}^{-1}]{\operatorname{sky}} 
  \left\{ \begin{tabular}{c} Gabriel open \\ sets of $\operatorname{Sp}(P^{\sigma})$ \end{tabular}  \right\}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
For the first bijection, combine Proposition \ref{Prop:OneSideInverseForSuppSets} and Theorem \ref{Thm:OneSideInverseForLocSubCat}. 
The second one is a consequence of Theorem \ref{Thm:ForSobSpaceGabrielIsSkula}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{Prop:Easy}
Let $P = \mathbb{R}$. 
Then the following hold: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item the Scott sheaf $j_*k[p,q]$ is not finitely presented for any $p < q$; 
    \item $j^* \mathcal{F}$ is a finitely presented persistence module over $\mathbb{R}$, when $\mathcal{F}$ is a finitely presented Scott sheaf on $\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}$; 
    \item a Scott sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}$ is finitely presented if and only if $\mathcal{F} = 0$; 
    \item $\mathbf{Sh}(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ is not locally finitely presented. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
(i) 
Consider the directed system $(j_*k[x,q])_{p < x < q}$ of subsheaves of $j_*k[p,q]$. 
Clearly, 
\[
  \operatorname{Hom}(j_*k[p,q], j_*k[x,q]) 
  = \operatorname{Hom}(k[p,q], j^!j_*k[x,q]) 
  = \operatorname{Hom}(k[p,q], k[x,q[) 
  = 0
\]
for all $p < x < q$. 
But 
\[
  \operatorname{Hom} \left(j_*k[p,q], \varinjlim_{p < x < q} j_*k[x,q] \right) 
  = \operatorname{Hom}(j_*k[p,q], j_*k[p,q]) 
  \cong k. 
\]
Hence, $j_*k[p,q]$ is not finitely presented.

(ii) 
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented Scott sheaf on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $(M_{i})_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of persistence modules over $\mathbb{R}$. 
Since $(j^*, j_*, j^!)$ is an adjoint triple and $j_*$ preserves direct limits, we have 
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Hom} \left(j^* \mathcal{F}, \varinjlim_{i \in I} M_i \right) 
  &= \operatorname{Hom} \left(\mathcal{F}, j_* \varinjlim_{i \in I} M_i \right) 
  = \operatorname{Hom} \left(\mathcal{F}, \varinjlim_{i \in I} j_*M_i \right) \\
  &= \varinjlim_{i \in I} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{F}, j_*M_i) 
  = \varinjlim_{i \in I} \operatorname{Hom}(j^*\mathcal{F}, M_i). 
\end{align*}

(iii) 
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented Scott sheaf on $\mathbb{R}$. 
By (ii), $j^* \mathcal{F}$ is a finitely presented persistence module over $\mathbb{R}$. 
Lerch showed that $j^* \mathcal{F}$ must then be of the form $\bigoplus_{i = 1}^n k[p_i, q_i[$ for some $p_i < q_i$ ($i = 1, \dots, n$) (\cite[Lemma 3.6]{LerchSpectrum}). 
Thus, 
\[
  \mathcal{F} 
  = j_* j^* \mathcal{F} 
  = j_* \bigoplus_{i = 1}^n k \left[ p_i, q_i \right[ 
  = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^n j_*k[p_i, q_i]. 
\]
By (i), this cannot be finitely presented unless $\mathcal{F} = 0$. 

(iv) This is an immediate consequence of (iii).
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{Lemma:IndZieglerSubbasis}
\hfill
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item The open induced Ziegler spectrum $\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ is generated by the families of sets 
    
    \[\{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x \le p \} \quad \text{and} \quad \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x > p \},\] where $p \in \mathbb{R}$; 
    \item The closed induced Ziegler spectrum $\operatorname{Zg}^c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ is generated by the families of sets 
    \[\{ k\left] -\infty, x\right] \in \operatorname{Zg}^c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x < p \} \quad \text{and} \quad \{ k\left] -\infty, x\right] \in \operatorname{Zg}^c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x \ge p \},\] where $p \in \mathbb{R}$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
(i) 
The Ziegler topology of persistence modules is generated by the families of sets $\{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid D \subsetneq F \}$ and $\{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid F \subsetneq D \}$, where $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is an ideal. 

Suppose first that $F$ is open in the standard topology, so that $F = \left]-\infty, p\right[$ for some $p \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{ \infty \}$. The intersections with $\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ are then simply 
\begin{align*}
  \{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid D \subsetneq \left] -\infty, p\right[ \,\} \cap \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) 
  &= \{ \, k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid \left]-\infty, x\right[ \subsetneq \left]-\infty, p\right[ \, \} \\
  &= \{ \, k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x < p \}
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
  \{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid \left] -\infty, p\right[ \subsetneq D \} \cap \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) 
  &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid \left]-\infty, p\right[ \subsetneq \left]-\infty, x\right[ \, \} \\
  &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid p < x \}. 
\end{align*}

Now suppose that $F=\left]-\infty,p\right]$ for some $p \in \mathbb{R}$. Then  
\begin{align*}
  \{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid \left] -\infty, p\right] \subsetneq D \} \cap \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) 
  &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid \left]-\infty, p\right] \subsetneq \left]-\infty, x\right[ \, \} \\
  &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[\in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid p < x \} 
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
  \{ k[D] \in \operatorname{InjSpec}(\mathbb{R}^a) \mid D \subsetneq \left] -\infty, p\right] \, \} \cap \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) 
    &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid \left]-\infty, x\right[ \subseteq \left]-\infty, p\right[ \, \} \\ 
  &= \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x \le p \}. 
\end{align*}

From these computations, we see that the families of sets \[ \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x \le p \}\quad\text{and}\quad \{ k\left]-\infty, x\right[ \in \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \mid x > p \}, \] where $p \in \mathbb{R}$, generate the open induced Ziegler topology on $\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$.

(ii) The argument is analogous.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{Thm:InducedZieglerSpectrumsHomeo} Let $P=\mathbb{R}$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)] 
    \item The map \[ I_c \colon \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}\to\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^\sigma) \] is a homeomorphism, where $\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ is endowed with the Sorgenfrey topology, that is, the topology generated by the intervals $]x,y]$ with $x<y$. 
    
    \item The map \[ I^c \colon \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}\to\operatorname{Zg}^c(\mathbb{R}^\sigma) \] is a homeomorphism, where $\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ is endowed with the topology generated by the intervals $[x, \infty]$ ja $\left] - \infty , y\right[$. \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
(i)
By Lemma~\ref{Lemma:IndZieglerSubbasis} (i), the generating families of $\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^\sigma)$ correspond under $I_c$ to the families \[ \{\, \left]-\infty,p \right] \mid p\in\mathbb{R}\,\} \quad\text{and}\quad \{\, \left]p,\infty\right[\mid p\in\mathbb{R}\,\}, \] which generate the Sorgenfrey topology.
Hence $I_c$ is a homeomorphism.

(ii) The proof is analogous.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{Cor:OpenIndZieglerHomeoGabriel}
Let $P = \mathbb{R}$. 
The open induced Ziegler spectrum and the Gabriel spectrum are homeomorphic: 
\[
  \operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}) \approx \operatorname{Sp}(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma}). 
\]
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
By Theorems \ref{Thm:GabrielSpecOfScottShOverR} and \ref{Thm:InducedZieglerSpectrumsHomeo} (i), both the Gabriel spectrum $\operatorname{Sp}(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ and the open induced Ziegler spectrum $\operatorname{Zg}_c(\mathbb{R}^{\sigma})$ are homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ endowed with the Sorgenfrey topology.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
Let $P = \mathbb{R}$. 
Note that the Ziegler spectrum and the Gabriel spectrum of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb{R}, \mathbf{Mod})$ are not homeomorphic: 
\[
  \operatorname{Zg}(\mathbb{R}^a) \not\approx \operatorname{Sp}(\mathbb{R}^a). 
\]
The difference is caused by the ephemeral modules. 
Indeed, Proposition \ref{Prop:GabrielSpecOfDenseLinPoset} shows that the Gabriel spectrum contains many open points due to ephemeral modules. 
However, ephemeral modules are not finitely presented (\cite[Lemma 3.6]{LerchSpectrum}), and therefore they do not contribute to the Ziegler spectrum.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
